perspective:
From Sara Manuelito’s available perspective:

- Sara knows Shirley as a long-time colleague and close friend from their work at a community health center; Shirley is a nurse, and Sara is a speech-language pathologist.
- Sara knows they shared care for a mutual patient who has died, and she attends the patient’s funeral at a funeral parlour/place of worship/ceremony.
- At the funeral, Sara observes Shirley’s somber demeanor and suspects Shirley is deeply affected. She hears Shirley say it has been tough, that she keeps thinking something more could have been done, and that it is hard to let go. Sara says they did everything they could and should remember the good care and moments of joy.
- During a work coffee break, Sara raises the topic of treatment decisions and says she senses Shirley may feel burdened. She hears Shirley say she feels responsible, wonders if pushing for a different approach might have helped, and finds it hard to accept. Sara says they made the best decisions with the information they had and that Shirley should not carry the burden alone.
- In their office, Sara observes Shirley continuing to be reserved and minimally expressive. Sara tells Shirley she has noticed she is holding back feelings and that it is okay to be open. She hears Shirley say she does not want to seem unprofessional or weak. Sara says expressing emotion is not weak and is healthy among friends. Shirley says maybe Sara is right and she will try to be more open.
- Later, Sara feels her previous confrontation may have been too harsh and apologizes if she came on too strong. Shirley says it was a bit much but that Sara meant well and accepts the apology. Sara offers support; Shirley says continuing to talk helps.
- After some time, Sara observes that Shirley seems to be doing better and feels hopeful. She asks how Shirley is feeling. Shirley says she is better, thanks to their talks and Sara’s support. Sara suggests spending more time together outside work; Shirley agrees to plan something for the weekend.

Sara does not have access to Shirley’s private thoughts or feelings beyond what Shirley states or what Sara observes/infers from her behavior.
